Description

This PR is part of a series in which I update the Learn area "Challenge" articles. In general, they need to be modernized, restructured, and put in better positions in the modules so they are spaced out better and test subjects that have already been covered.

In this PR specifically, I update the Fundamental layout comprehension challenge to:

  • Improve the HTML, CSS, and JS code in general.
  • Bring the article structure more in line with what I've been doing in other places, for example, consistent structure and reducing reliance on the learning-area repo
  • Moving the article to just after the grid content, as that means it sits just after the items it tests. I am intending to create a separate challenge to test some of these techniques combined with RWD (media queries, etc.)

Motivation

items.content_html:
Description

Chrome 140 adds support for CSS typed arithmetic; see https://chromestatus.com/feature/4740780497043456.

It is not very clear what this is from the spec, but https://css-tricks.com/css-typed-arithmetic/ provides a good explanation.

This PR specifically:

  • Adds a guide under the CSS values and units module explaining what it is, and showing some examples.
  • Adds short sections to the function pages that this new behavior is relevant to (calc(). abs() and sign() for now, although other functions might be relevant too), and edits any mentions of typed arithmetic rules that are rendered out-of-date by this update.

Motivation

Additional details

items.content_html:
Description

This PR fixes the “Ordered list” example on the sibling-index() documentation page.

Motivation

The bug: The old example set content: var(--list-index); where --list-index was just an integer. The CSS content property does not accept raw numbers, so the pseudo-element would render nothing.

The fix: By introducing a CSS counter (counter-set + counter()), the numeric value from sibling-index() is converted into a valid, displayable string.

Additional details

Related issues and pull requests

Fixes #41290
items.title: #41290 CSS: Fix sibling-index() example to use counters with content

items.content_html:
Add reference for CSS value serialization, especially colors

Fixes #32734

Description

Adds a new guide explaining CSS value serialization through JavaScript APIs, with a focus on how color values (hsl(), hwb(), etc.) are serialized to rgb()/rgba() format when accessed via getComputedStyle() or getPropertyValue().

Motivation

This documentation helps developers understand why and how CSS values, especially colors, might return in different formats than they were written. This addresses a common source of confusion when working with CSS values through JavaScript APIs.

Additional details

References:

  • CSSOM Specification - Serializing CSS Values
  • CSS Color Module Level 4 - Serialization

Related issues and pull requests

Fixes #32734 - Creates documentation for CSS value serialization, especially for colors
items.title: docs: Add reference for CSS value serialization, especially colors

items.content_html:
Description

Chrome 136 introduces the CSS dynamic-range-limit property; see https://chromestatus.com/feature/5146250411769856.

The dynamic-range-limit-mix() function is also supported, but I'm not sure which version of Chrome this first appeared in. I've asked Chrome engineering for an answer to this question.

This PR documents both of the two features mentioned above.

Note

Some of the description in the property page might want to go into a separate glossary entry, but I wasn't sure how best to chop up this information. Opinions welcome.

Motivation

Additional details

Related issues and pull requests
items.title: Editorial review: Document CSS dynamic-range-limit

items.content_html:
FF144 (and Safari) implement CSSStyleProperties. This is a derived class of CSSStyleDeclaration that represents the inline or computed styles on an element. It exists because CSSStyleDeclaration is now going to be a base class from which specific types of style and rule information will be applied, and only include the relevant information for that context.

Anyway, this adds the new class and fixes up all the places that return it. It also updates CSSStyleDeclaration to note that this is now a base class but didn't used to be.

There is quite a lot of duplication. Mostly because there was before I started too. I wasn't sure how much to include in say HTMLElement.style and how much to have in the CSSStyleProperties as common. Generally I have kept about the same level in each doc as originally.

Related docs work can be tracked in #41133
items.title: FF144 CSSStyleProperties docs
